What is the equation of the ellipse given above?

{{field-1}}$=1$
question.worked_solution:
Remember that the general equation of an ellipse centered at $(h,k)$ with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

Here, the ellipse is centered at $(2,-2),$ the horizontal radius has length $a=2,$ and the vertical radius has length $b=1.$ Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{{2}^{2}}+\frac{(y-(-2))^{2}}{{1}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{4}+(y+2)^{2} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
